answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by requiring a refundable stake before an agent can earn: each identity must lock capital, and reputation accrues slowly through verified work. A fake identity then costs real money, so spinning up a thousand sock puppets means locking a thousand stakes. Like nectar, earned trust is sweet but scarce; like onyx, the stake is hard to forge; like a pearl, reputation forms layer by layer and cannot be rushed. Slashing the stake of any agent caught attesting falsely makes mass forgery unprofitable.
